'''Stephan Albani''' (born 3 June 1968 in [[Göttingen]]) is a German politician of the [[Christian Democratic Union of Germany|Christian Democratic Union]] (CDU) who has been a [[Member of the German Bundestag|member]] of the German [[Bundestag]] since the [[2013 German federal election|federal election in 2013]].<ref name="bt">[https://www.bundestag.de/abgeordnete/biografien/A/albani_stephan/517864 Stephan Albani, CDU/CSU], Bundestag.de</ref>

==Early life and education==
Albani was born in [[Göttingen]], and graduated from high school in 1987 in [[Norderstedt]]. From 1989 to 1994 he studied physics at the [[Georg-August-Universität Göttingen]] with a degree as Diplomphysiker.

==Career in the private sector==
Albani was a managing partner of Hörzentrum (''Hearing Center'') GmbH [[Oldenburg (city)|Oldenburg]] from 1996 and managing director of HörTech gGmbH Oldenburg from 2001.<ref name="bt"/> The shareholders of the HörTech GmbH competence centre are the [[University of Oldenburg]] and Hörzentrum Oldenburg GmbH.<ref>{{cite news |last1= |first1= |title="Universität Oldenburg beteiligt sich an Kapitalgesellschaft – Ziel: Entwicklung neuer Hörgeräte" |url=https://idw-online.de/de/news?print=1&id=41489 |access-date=27 March 2025 |work=idw-online.de |date=15 November 2001 |language=de}}</ref> He relinquished this position in 2018.<ref>{{cite news |last1= |first1= |title="Führungswechsel nach 20 Jahren" |url=https://www.nwzonline.de/wirtschaft/oldenburg-wissenschaft-fuehrungswechsel-nach-ueber-20-jahren_a_50,3,3452263370.html |access-date=27 March 2025 |work=nwzonline.de |date=28 January 2019 |language=de}}</ref>

He is a member of the Federal Association for Economic Development and Foreign Trade (BWA [[European Movement Germany|EBD]]) and was Vice-President from 2007 to 2021.<ref>{{cite news |last1= |first1= |title="Das Präsidium" |url=https://www.bwa-deutschland.com/praesidium |access-date=27 March 2025 |work=bwa-deutschland.com |date=11 May 2020 |language=de |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200511125600/https://www.bwa-deutschland.com/praesidium |archive-date=11 May 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Coordes |first1=Nils |title="CDU-Politiker Stephan Albani reagiert auf Russland-Vorwürfe" |url=https://www.nwzonline.de/politik/einfluss-auf-abgeordnetestephan-albani-reagiert-auf-russland-vorwuerfe-marcus-held-alexander-kulitz-stefan-keuter-cdu-spd-fdp-afd-bwa_a_51,1,1123680747.html |access-date=27 March 2025 |work=nwzonline.de |date=7 May 2021 |language=de}}</ref> and became head of the Innovation Commission in Berlin in 2007.<ref name="Berlin1">{{cite news |last1= |first1= |title="Stephan Albani" |url=https://digital-health-symposium.de/wp-content/uploads/2020/09/200917-Lebenslauf_Stephan-Albani-MdB.pdf |access-date=27 March 2025 |work=digital-health-symposium.de |date= |language=de}}</ref> In the same year, Albani became managing director of the Auditory Valley [[German Universities Excellence Initiative|excellence initiative]] cluster and held this position until 2018.<ref name="Berlin2">{{cite news |last1= |first1= |title="Stephan Albani" |url=https://www.bundestag.de/abgeordnete/biografien/A/albani_stephan-857088 |access-date=27 March 2025 |work=bundestag.de |date= |language=de}}</ref> In 2008, the state initiative Innovatives Niedersachsen - Zukunft schmieden (Innovative Lower Saxony - Forging the Future) entrusted him with the deputy management of the Health and Nutrition working group in Hanover.<ref name="Berlin1" /> In the same year, he became an [[Procuration|authorised signatory]] of the [[Community health center|Medical Care Centre]] at the Evangelical Hospital in Oldenburg.<ref>{{cite news |last1= |first1= |title="Medizinzentrum setzt auf gesundes Wachstum" |url=https://www.nwzonline.de/kultur/oldenburg-klinik-medizinzentrum-setzt-auf-gesundes-wachstum_a_1,0,3243110117.html |access-date=27 March 2025 |work=nwzonline.de |date=6 November 2009 |language=de}}</ref>

In 2010, Lower Saxony's State Ministry of Economic Affairs appointed Albani to the advisory board of the Lower Saxony State Initiative LifeSciences in Hanover, where he remained until he became a member of the Bundestag.<ref name="Hanover1">{{cite news |last1= |first1= |title="Stephan Albani" |url=https://www.cducsu.de/abgeordnete/stephan-albani |access-date=27 March 2025 |work= |date= |language=de}}</ref>

From 2011 to 2013, Albani headed the health working group of the state initiative Innovatives Niedersachsen - Zukunft schmieden of Lower Saxony's State Ministry of Economic Affairs in Hanover.<ref name="Berlin1" /> 
As part of the Cluster of Excellence Hearing4All, he took over the Translational Research Centre (TRC) management. The background to this was the successful application by the University of Oldenburg, with [[Hannover Medical School]] and [[Leibniz University Hannover]], for the Cluster of Excellence Hearing4All in June 2012. The TRC is tasked with translating the results of the cluster's research work into products.<ref name="Berlin1" /> He headed the programme until 2018.<ref name="Hanover1" />

In 2020, Albani gave lectures on [[Rib cage|thoracic]] surgery and [[lung cancer]] for [[AstraZeneca]], earning between 1,000 and 3,500 euros.<ref name="Hanover2">{{cite news |last1= |first1= |title="Stephan Albani" |url=https://www.abgeordnetenwatch.de/profile/stephan-albani/nebentaetigkeiten?sidejob_keys=&legislatures_of_politician_sidejobs=All&category=All&field_topics_target_id=&income_level=All&interval=All&order=created&sort=desc&page=1 |access-date=27 March 2025 |work=abgeordnetenwatch.de |date= |language=de}}</ref>

==Political career==
[[File:2020-02-14 Deutscher Bundestag IMG 3641 by Stepro.jpg|thumb|Albani in the plenum of the [[German Bundestag]]]]
Albani is deputy chairman of the Ammerland CDU district association and the Bad Zwischenahn CDU town association.<ref name="Berlin2" /> He became a member of the [[Economic Council Germany|CDU Economic Council]] in 2009 and was involved in the Innovation and Growth working group in Berlin.<ref name="Berlin1" />

In July 2012, Albani was nominated by the CDU as a [[Direktmandat|direct candidate]] for the [[Oldenburg – Ammerland|parliamentary constituency of Oldenburg – Ammerland]],<ref name="Berlin1" /> but missed out on the direct mandate with 36.8% of the first votes.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Buck |first1=Patrick |title="Das sind die Ziele der Bundestags-Bewerber" |url=https://www.nwzonline.de/politik/oldenburg-nwz-fragt-kandidaten-antworten-das-sind-die-ziele-der-bundestags-bewerber_a_32,0,3517664719.html |access-date=27 March 2025 |work=nwzonline.de |date=14 September 2017 |language=de}}</ref> Nevertheless, he entered the Bundestag in the [[2013 German federal election|2013 federal election]]<ref name="Berlin2" /> in 6th place on the CDU state list for Lower Saxony.<ref>{{cite news |last1= |first1= |title="Oldenburger Kandidaten abgesichert – Erstmals 4 Oldenburger Bundestagsabgeordnete möglich" |url=https://web.cdu-ol.de/2012/2523/ |access-date=27 March 2025 |work=web.cdu-ol.de |date=3 November 2012 |language=de}}</ref> During the 18th legislative period, he was a full member of the Committee on Education, Research and Technology Assessment and a deputy member of the Committee on Health. He was also Chairman of the German-[[Southeast Europe|South-East European]] Parliamentary Group from 2016 to 2017.<ref name="Berlin2" />

In 2014, Albani was appointed to the CDU's Federal Committee on Education, Research and Innovation, having already spent several years as head of the 'Science, Culture, Church' committee of the CDU's Oldenburg regional association. He is also involved in the two specialised committees' Science and Culture' and 'Health' of the CDU Lower Saxony. Since 2018, he has been an assessor on the federal board of the Mittelstands- und Wirtschaftsunion.<ref>{{cite news |last1= |first1= |title="STEPHAN ALBANI MDB" |url=https://www.mit-bund.de/content/stephan-albani-mdb |access-date=27 March 2025 |work=mit-bund.de |date= |language=de}}</ref><ref name="Berlin2" />

In the [[2017 German federal election|2017 Bundestag election]], he again missed out on the direct mandate in his constituency with 30.2% of the first votes. He again entered the Bundestag via the sixth place on the Lower Saxony CDU list. In the 19th legislative period, he was a full member of the Study Commission on Vocational Training in the Digital World of Work and the Committee on Education, Research and Technology Assessment. He was also a deputy member of the Committee on Health, the Committee on Labour and Social Affairs<ref name="Berlin2" /> and the Subcommittee on Global Health.

In addition to his committee assignments, Albani served as chairman of the German-Irish Parliamentary Friendship Group from 2017 to 2021.<ref>{{cite news |last1= |first1= |title="Deutsch-Irische Parlamentariergruppe" |url=https://www.bundestag.de/webarchiv/presse/pressemitteilungen/2019/646264-646264 |access-date=27 March 2025 |work=bundestag.de |date=6 June 2019 |language=de}}</ref> He was also a member of the SADC parliamentary group, the Nordic parliamentary group and the CDU/CSU parliamentary group's Stephanus Circle.

In the [[2021 German federal election|2021 Bundestag elections]], he missed out on a direct mandate with 19.9% of the first votes in his constituency and entered parliament in 11th place on the Lower Saxony state list. In the 20th legislative period, he is the spokesperson for his parliamentary group on the Committee on Education, Research and Technology Assessment and a full member of the Subcommittee on Global Health. He is also a deputy member of the Committee on Health and Chairman of the [[Egypt-Germany relations|German-Egyptian Parliamentary Group]].<ref>{{cite news |last1= |first1= |title="Deutsch-Ägyptische Parlamentariergruppe zu Gesprächen in Kairo und Assuan" |url=https://www.bundestag.de/presse/pressemitteilungen/2024/pm-240201-reise-kairo-988562 |access-date=27 March 2025 |work=bundestag.de |date=1 February 2024 |language=de}}</ref> Albani is also a member of the Parliamentary Network to Combat [[Tuberculosis]]<ref>{{cite news |last1= |first1= |title="Welttuberkulosetag 2018: Albani mahnt zu mehr politischem Engagement gegen die tödlichste Infektionskrankheit" |url=https://stephan-albani.de/press/welttuberkulosetag-2018-albani-mahnt-zu-mehr-politischem-engagement-gegen-die-toedlichste-infektionskrankheit/ |access-date=27 March 2025 |work=stephan-albani.de |date=23 March 2018 |language=de}}</ref> and was a full member of the Parliamentary Monitoring Committee on the COVID-19 pandemic in 2021.<ref>{{cite news |last1= |first1= |title="Stephan Albani plant jetzt bei Pandemie-Maßnahmen mit" |url=https://www.nwzonline.de/ammerland/ammerland-berlin-abgeordneter-mitglied-im-corona-ausschuss-stephan-albani-plant-jetzt-bei-pandemie-massnahmen-mit_a_51,0,2551306183.html |access-date=27 March 2025 |work=nwzonline.de |date=26 March 2021 |language=de}}</ref>

==Political positions==
Albani is one of his parliamentary group's 75 MPs who voted against the party line and in favour of [[same-sex marriage]] in July 2017.<ref>{{cite news |last1= |first1= |title="Diese Unionsabgeordneten stimmen für die Ehe für alle" |url=https://www.welt.de/politik/deutschland/article166099805/Diese-Unionsabgeordneten-stimmten-fuer-die-Ehe-fuer-alle.html |access-date=27 March 2025 |work=welt.de |date=30 June 2017 |language=de}}</ref>

==Controversy==
Albani earned between 1,000 and 7,000 euros per month from his sideline activities at Hörzentrum Oldenburg and HörTech.<ref name="Oldenburg1">{{cite news |last1= |first1= |title="Stephan Albani" |url=https://www.bundestag.de/webarchiv/abgeordnete/biografien19/A/albani_stephan-517864 |access-date=27 March 2025 |work=bundestag.de |date= |language=de}}</ref> A Transparency study identified a potential conflict of interest between Albani's activities and reporting on 'accelerating the transfer of research results and innovations into healthcare'.<ref name="Oldenburg1"/>
On 17 August 2017, the Nordwest-Zeitung reported on Albani's activities.<ref>{{cite news |last1= |first1= |title="Stephan Albani: "Dann falle ich ins Bodenlose"" |url=https://www.nwzonline.de/niedersachsen/stephan-albani-nebeneinkuenfte-abgeordnete_a_32,0,2253251856.html# |access-date=27 March 2025 |work=nwzonline.de |date=15 August 2017 |language=de}}</ref> According to Martin Reyher from [[Parliamentwatch|abgeordnetenwatch.de]], it was 'quite obvious' that Albani, as a member of the Committee on Health and the Committee on Education, Research and Technology Assessment of the German Bundestag, was co-deciding on taxpayers' money, from which he potentially benefited through his sideline activities as managing director of federally funded companies. Lobbycontrol also described Albani's sideline activities as a 'clear case of bias'. In an interview with the newspaper, Albani stated that he 'only assisted the two companies in an advisory capacity for 3 to 4 hours a week' and had thus recorded gross additional income of just under €42,000 in 2016. The continuation of the companies alongside his parliamentary mandate is an economic necessity: if he were to leave the Bundestag, 'then I would fall into a bottomless pit'. Albani was also criticised in letters to the editor of the Nordwest-Zeitung,<ref>{{cite news |last1= |first1= |title="Verständnis und Kritik an Nebenverdienst" |url=https://www.nwzonline.de/leserbriefe/verstaendnis-und-kritik-an-nebenverdienst_a_32,0,2832980977.html |access-date=27 March 2025 |work=nwzonline.de |date=26 August 2017 |language=de}}</ref> and Albani responded to the accusations on his website,<ref>{{cite news |last1= |first1= |title="ÜBER MICH" |url=https://stephan-albani.de/albani/ |access-date=27 March 2025 |work=stephan-albani.de |date= |language=de}}</ref> where he once again emphasised that it was necessary to continue running the companies in the event of his resignation from the Bundestag. He rejected the accusation of bias in the committee's work.<ref name="Oldenburg1" /> In 2018, he ended all his economic activities. In 2020, he received remuneration of between 3,500 and 7,000 euros for consultancy work for HörTech gGmbH.

==Memberships==
Albani was Vice President of the Federal Association for Economic Development and Foreign Trade (BWA) until 2021, which, according to research by the ARD political magazine Kontraste and [[Die Zeit]], maintains lobbying contacts with individuals and organisations with close ties to Russian oligarch [[Yevgeny Prigozhin]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Becker |first1=Andrea |last2=Heil |first2=Georg |last3=Pohl |first3=Markus |title=""Putins Koch" und sein langer Arm" |url=https://www.tagesschau.de/investigativ/kontraste/putin-koch-101.html |access-date=27 March 2025 |work=tagesschau.de |date=6 May 2021 |language=de}}</ref> He has been Co-Chairman of the European TB Caucus since 2015.
He is a board member of the GeWiNet competence centre for the healthcare industry.<ref name="Hanover2" />
He is a member of the [[Rotary International|Rotary Club]], Bundeswehr-Sozialwerk, and the nonpartisan [[Europa-Union Deutschland]], which is committed to a federal Europe and the European unification process.<ref>{{cite news |last1= |first1= |title="Europa-Union Parlamentarier im 19. Deutschen Bundestag (2017-2121)" |url=https://www.europa-union.de/ueber-uns/parlamentariergruppen/deutscher-bundestag-19-wp/a-z-19-bt |access-date=27 March 2025 |work=europa-union.de |date= |language=de}}</ref> He is also a member of the Freundeskreis Korvette [[German corvette Oldenburg|Oldenburg]],<ref>{{cite news |last1= |first1= |title="Bundeswehr als Gastgeber" |url=https://www.nwzonline.de/oldenburg/bundeswehr-als-gastgeber_a_6,1,791165943.html |access-date=27 March 2025 |work=nwzonline.de |date=5 March 2016 |language=de}}</ref> which aims to maintain the sponsorship of the German Navy ship of the same name.

==Other activities==
* [[Studentenwerk|German National Association for Student Affairs]], Ex-Officio Member of the Board of Trustees (since 2022)<ref>[https://www.studentenwerke.de/en/content/board-trustees-deutsches-studentenwerk Board of Trustees] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220402064738/https://www.studentenwerke.de/en/content/board-trustees-deutsches-studentenwerk |date=2 April 2022 }} [[Studentenwerk|German National Association for Student Affairs]].</ref>
* [[Helmholtz Association of German Research Centres]], Ex-Officio Member of the Senate (since 2022)<ref>[https://www.helmholtz.de/en/about-us/structure-and-governance/statutes-and-governance/senate/members-of-the-senate/ Senate, as of February 2022] [[Helmholtz Association of German Research Centres]].</ref><ref>[https://www.bundestag.de/dokumente/textarchiv/2022/kw07-de-wahl-gremien-879542 Mitglieder mehrerer Gremien gewählt] [[Bundestag]], press release of 17 February 2022.</ref>
* Eurasian Parliamentary Group on TB (EPGTB), Co-Chairman (since 2016)<ref>[https://www.globaltbcaucus.org/single-post/2016/08/17/Latest-news-%E2%80%93-Launch-of-the-Eurasian-Parliamentary-Group-on-TB Launch of the Eurasian Parliamentary Group on TB] Global TB Caucus, press release of 27 June 2016.</ref>
* [[EWE Baskets Oldenburg]], Member of the Advisory Board<ref>[http://ewe-baskets.de/club/aufsichtsrat-beirat/index.html Advisory Board] [[EWE Baskets Oldenburg]].</ref>
* [[German Foundation for World Population]] (DSW), Member of the Parliamentary Advisory Board<ref>[https://www.dsw.org/parlamentarischer-beirat/ Advisory Board] [[German Foundation for World Population]] (DSW).</ref>
* German Military Reserve Association, Member
* Bundeswehr-Sozialwerk, Member
* [[OFFIS|Oldenburg Institute for Information Technology]] (OFFIS), Member of the Supervisory Board
* German Medical Technology Alliance (GMTA), Member of the Board (2004-2013)

==Personal life==
Albani is married, [[Protestantism|Protestant]], has three children and lives in [[Petersfehn]] in [[Ammerland]], where he is deputy chairman of his party.<ref name="bt"/>
